top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Krk Gran Fondo. Practice on rolling island roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 51 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Krk Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
When someone attacks on rolling island roads, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
85ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Krk Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
At Krk Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Krk Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
51 miles on rolling island roads burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on rolling island roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Varied gradients on rolling island roads demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Smooth pedaling at 51 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
Base fitness for Krk Gran Fondo. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
